written. - this regulation lays down rules for the accurate monitoring, verification and reporting of carbon dioxide (co2) emissions from ships calling at or departing from ports under the jurisdiction of a member state in order to promote the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions from maritime transport in a cost-effective manner. the commission proposal introduces four basic methods for measuring co2 emissions, covering 98% of all emissions from ships. the commission notes that the commission did not provide any information on the amount of the compensation for the ships concerned. however, the permitted weight was significantly reduced following the vote in the envi committee in january this year, nox reporting was added and the permitted limit was lowered to 400 gross tonnes. accordingly, i did not support this report as the amendments mentioned would represent a significant burden for smaller ship owners to implement and the measures are not proportionate in terms of reducing emissions.
written. - the european union's environment is extremely diverse, with over ten thousand alien species in the union (of which about 40% are imported from other member states), and it is estimated that about one in ten are invasive. the risks and concerns associated with invasive alien species pose a problem not only for the member state into which the alien species has been introduced, but also for the union as a whole. it is therefore essential to introduce a prohibition at union level on the introduction of invasive alien species into any member state in order to ensure a harmonised action throughout the union and thus avoid disturbances in the internal market and prevent situations where measures taken in one member state are jeopardised by the lack of action in another member state. that is why i support this regulation, in particular the parts relating to stricter rules in the member states, the introduction of effective and proportionate penalties for infringements and the establishment of a scientific forum with an advisory function on scientific issues related to the regulation.
written. - alien species have been pushed out of their natural range across ecological barriers by direct or indirect human action. some of these species can't adapt to their new environment and they need help. invasive species (hereinafter 'irps') are those that are identified as being lacking in ecosystem biodiversity or as having a negative impact on the environment, human health and socio-economic development. mrs includes animals, plants, fungi and micro-organisms, and impacts on continental land and water surfaces and eu seas and islands. as early as 2009, the european parliament and the environment council supported eu strategies. the mrs was one of the 10 priority objectives of the biodiversity action plan. the negative impact requires coordinated action at union level and will be compiled by the european commission in cooperation with the member states. member states will have to take measures to secure those species that are not introduced and are traded. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the application of this regulation.
written. - the risks and concerns associated with invasive alien species represent a transnational problem affecting the union as a whole. accordingly, i supported this report as it is essential to introduce a union-wide prohibition on the deliberate introduction into the union, reproduction, farming, transport, purchase, sale, use, exchange, possession and release of invasive alien species of union concern in order to ensure early and coordinated action across the union and thus avoid disruption of the internal market and prevent situations where measures taken in one member state are jeopardised by the failure to take action in another member state.

written. - the question of whether pollen is a natural ingredient or an integral part of honey is, at first glance, absurd and irrelevant. but it is a decision that could have far-reaching consequences for the future of the beekeeping sector in europe. i'll throw out all the arguments and endorse the view that pollen is one of the ingredients of honey. why would you do that? firstly, because i believe that european consumers must have the right to know whether the honey they consume contains gmos. because if pollen is an ingredient, then honey that contains pollen from a gmo plant must have that indicated on the label. in addition to consumer rights, we will also protect the producers of honey that produce honey without gmo components, which is the majority of european beekeepers. i disagree with the european commission's proposal that pollen is an integral part of honey because it goes to the gmos industry, the honey wholesalers and the importers. when it comes to choosing between short-term profit and long-term security, i will always vote for security and the consumer's right to know what they're buying.
written. - the commission's proposal is to supplement closely directive 2001/110/ec on honey by defining pollen as an ingredient of honey. it's an attempt to push genetically modified food into the diet without informing the public. in fact, eu labelling rules for genetically modified foods state that the declaration must be labelled if the article contains more than 0.9% gm content. however, if we consider that pollen is a natural ingredient of honey, this threshold is not exceeded, even if it is exclusively from gm crops, because pollen in the concentration of honey is never higher than 0,5%. i am totally against this proposal and i am extremely concerned about the health of citizens, but also of small producers in the union who continue to produce in a natural way. as a representative of the people, my goal is to advocate for the interests of croatian citizens and protect future generations. i also want to acknowledge the efforts of croatian beekeepers who are making great efforts to produce natural and safe honey. such work is not easy, and it requires a greater degree of responsibility and constant investment in education, facilities and other equipment, and the daily care of the bees. croatia is a gmo free country and i hope that the will of its citizens to keep it that way will be respected.
written. - i commend the efforts of rapporteur girling to bring sanity back to the business of beekeepers, mostly small and medium-sized enterprises, throughout europe. in particular, after the european court of justice ruled in 2011 that pollen is an ingredient of honey, the same decision caused costly and unnecessary complications for beekeepers who found themselves in the situation of having to relabel all honey and honey-containing products to indicate pollen as an ingredient in the same. the same practice has the potential to cost beekeepers eur 3,25 million, while undermining consumers' perception of honey as a natural product. as honey is a natural product, it should be exempted from the obligation to display the list of ingredients. that is why i voted for the amendment by rapporteur girling which calls for pollen to be considered not as an ingredient of honey but as a plant matter.

written. - maritime spatial planning and integrated coastal management will contribute to promoting the sustainable development of maritime and coastal economies and the sustainable use of marine and coastal resources, and to opportunities for public and private investment, which will have an impact on all sectoral policies related to maritime and coastal space. the maritime space as a key element for renewable energy sources, oil and gas exploration, maritime and fisheries activities, ecosystem and biodiversity conservation, aquaculture facilities, tourism and fisheries resources needs coordination, linking or integration of spatial plans, integrated strategies and coastal area management. this would ensure the sustainable use of maritime space and the management of coastal areas. but social, economic, and environmental factors and goals must also be considered. therefore, i agree with the european commission that member states must designate competent authorities responsible for cooperation with other member states or non-eu countries in order to implement as well as possible programmes and exchange of good practices that contribute to positive processes for the development of strategies and plans for coastal and maritime spatial management.

written. - i voted against because i believe that the commission proposal unnecessarily interferes with the competences of the member states of the union and in doing so violates the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. the proposal aims to establish a procedural framework for the creation and implementation of maritime spatial planning and integrated coastal management strategies in the member states of the union. the same processes are the exclusive competence of individual member states of the union, while the proposal calls for the union to assume minimum competences such as mutual coordination and integration, a six-yearly review and the consideration of all relevant marine and coastal activities. i firmly believe that maritime spatial planning is the exclusive competence of each member state of the union in particular and that union action in this segment should not be present even in the minimum requirements. i also object to the concept of "essential ecosystem components" because i believe that they would place an excessive and unnecessary burden on local government.

written. - each of europe's more than half a billion citizens generates more than half a tonne of waste per year in their homes every day, a huge number, not to mention the manufacturing and construction sectors. the european union as a whole produces around three billion tonnes of waste a year, which, as expected, creates a huge environmental problem, from pollution and greenhouse gas emissions that affect climate change, to financial and material costs. the commission should be able to verify that the waste is transported in a way that is compatible with the waste hierarchy. in order to contribute to the solution of this problem, the commission proposes that all member states make a publicly available inspection plan and set the strategy and objectives of inspections of waste shipments and the necessary resources. for environmental as well as economic reasons, i fully support the commission's objective and the rapporteur's proposals to further reinforce this objective, such as the proposal to make the plans and results of inspections by member states permanently available to the public, to increase the powers of the competent authorities and to increase cooperation between member states. i hope that this regulation will help us to tackle this environmental and economic problem in the context of increasing the efficiency and sustainability of the european union.

member of the commission. - madam president, honourable members of parliament, after five years of intensive negotiations, the chief negotiators have finished their work to deliver a comprehensive economic and trade agreement between the eu and canada. the committee on international trade (inta) immediately received the full text, and it will be made public shortly. canada is the first g8 member with whom we have agreed on a comprehensive trade deal. the agreement is crucial for the credibility of our trade agenda, because it confirms that we can do deals – even very good deals – in this case with a developed economy with its own established approach and regulatory framework. hence the challenging times during the negotiations. the agreement is also very valuable in its own right; it creates opportunities for our business. canada offers a sizeable market for european products and services. the operators get the same treatment, which is even better than that received by us competitors. this is an important achievement, sustaining our quest for more jobs and growth in europe when you consider the uncertain economic backdrop on our continent. politically, canada is an important ally. it is also an important destination for european investments, and it also invests massively in the eu, creating jobs and wealth. canada is rich in natural resources and raw materials and is a significant source of know-how. in short, through ceta, both sides will eliminate almost all customs tariffs (with very few exceptions). at the same time, a few very sensitive agricultural products will remain protected. the outcome concerning services and investment market access puts us on an even better footing than the us under nafta. it will also in no way affect the ability of eu governments at all levels to provide and subsidise public services. we have also achieved an unprecedented result on public procurement. under ceta we receive significant access to public procurement markets in canada at all levels of government. on investment, the agreement establishes a system that sets a new standard for investor-to-state dispute settlement procedures. we are well aware of the concerns that exist. this agreement directly addresses all the concerns that have emerged so far. also i want to highlight the result on geographical indications. we have achieved very extensive protection in canada of the designations of europe’s high-quality agricultural products, be they parmigiano reggiano, schwarzwälder schinken, bleu d’auvergne or 132 others which are fully protected. this is one of the parts which most visibly show how ceta can also benefit small and medium-sized operators across europe. the eu-canada trade and investment relationship will not come at the expense of environmental or social and labour standards. we are both aware that we have a responsibility here. we have a higher standard in trade agreements, and it is more than canada has done before. in terms of what happens next, president barroso and the canadian prime minister, mr harper, intend to publicly announce the conclusion of the negotiations at the eu-canada summit in ottawa on 26 september. further to this, both sides will submit this text to their respective legislators for verification and ratification. in the case of the eu this means to the council and parliament. because legal verification and official translations take so long, i would expect signature and formal transmission of the text to parliament to take place well into 2015. coming this far, at a pace which has been punishing for those involved, is an important achievement which the commission is proud of, and i look forward to this legislator’s support for ceta’s contribution to the creation of more jobs and growth in europe.
on behalf of the ecr club. madam president, we have already discussed in this session the negative effects of the cooling of relations with russia. while i'm afraid the latest russian bans on agricultural and food products are not the last we'll see from putin, this example does show clearly how damaging it can be to close a large market for our products and services. but despite the alarming situation in trade relations with russia, the european union has a fantastic opportunity to finally improve its relationship with the world's other great power and tempting market - canada. under this agreement, canada will open its public procurement market to european suppliers for the first time, and the expected increase in trade in goods and services of 23% should lead to a visible reduction in unemployment and an annual gain for the eu of more than eur 10 billion. this is great news for europe, which is in dire need of new partners on the global stage at this moment. i understand the reservations about isds, the legal safeguards, but i don't see them as justified. the isds instrument is also available in the united states for the purpose of the exchange of information between the member states and the commission. to my knowledge, there have been no problems so far which would lead to the conclusion that such an instrument is harmful to the member states. the isds balances the right and need of the state to regulate the market and the rights of investors to protection against possible arbitrariness or discriminatory behaviour of national governments towards foreign investors. the isds does not favour foreign capital over national sovereignty, as those who fear the application of this instrument think, but simply ensures respect for international law. i believe you will agree with me that the role of national government is not to oppose profit, but rather, by ensuring a level playing field in the market, it participates in its creation. the isds instrument provides private investors with a guarantee that national governments will indeed fulfil such a role, making the european market safer and thus more attractive to foreign investment. president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the recent ebola outbreak in west africa is the most important of its kind. this is a public health emergency of major international concern. the ebola outbreak is having an unprecedented public health and humanitarian impact on the affected countries and the entire region. the council is gravely concerned about the consequences for the socioeconomic and security situation of the west african countries affected. at the same time, we would remind you that according to the european centre for disease prevention and control, the risk of being infected by the ebola virus for residents of the european union and those travelling to the affected countries is low, provided that the recommended precautions are followed. the european union has taken a leading role within the international community in responding to the epidemic. at their meeting on 15 august, the foreign ministers called for a careful follow-up and a coordinated international response. the extraordinary european council of 30 august 2014 also stressed the importance of providing coordinated international support as quickly and effectively as possible. he called for greater coordination at eu level and called on the council to adopt a comprehensive eu response framework to deal with the situation. what was our follow-up in this case? as regards humanitarian aid, the european union and its member states have responded to the ebola crisis from the outset. this includes financial support to health and humanitarian actors and un organisations. we pay tribute to the extraordinary commitment of these field workers, commitment which some of them paid with their lives. in close coordination with the commission, member states have regularly carried out joint analyses and assessments of humanitarian assistance needs. the civil protection mechanism was activated at the request of who and the un office for the coordination of humanitarian affairs. the emergency response coordination centre, which is operational 24/7, contributes to the coordination of assistance. since the crisis has worsened, member states have stepped up their support and expressed their readiness to provide further assistance and to mobilise experts and medical staff. let me give you a few examples. the uk has started setting up a treatment centre near freetown, sierra leone, with the first phase expected to be operational within eight weeks. austria and france have offered in-kind assistance in the form of medical equipment. germany has taken in a who staff member who contracted the virus. italy has supported the world health organisation since the start of the crisis, making an initial contribution of eur 200 000 to the who's activities in guinea in april. a further eur 240 000 has recently been allocated. in addition, we have just approved a total of eur 1.2 million for the prevention and treatment of the virus. the council is currently working on a framework for the european union's overall response to the crisis. this framework will also address the coordination of air transport, which currently represents a critical gap and limits access for medical and humanitarian personnel and resources. the presidency is well aware of the need for more to be done. the eu must help rebuild health systems that have collapsed as a result of the ebola crisis. if we do not, there is a real risk that the humanitarian crisis caused by the ebola epidemic will spread to other countries on the african continent. the presidency, in conjunction with the commission and the eeas, will help coordinate the collective response of the european union in partnership with the who and the un. on the public health front, the eu response framework is in place and sufficient to protect human health in the union. eu member states have national preparedness plans to respond to possible health threats. at european level, member states, in cooperation with the commission, coordinate their responses to serious cross-border threats to health within the health security committee. a network of national competent authorities, the commission and the european centre for disease prevention and control, managed and coordinated by the ecdc, are responsible for the epidemiological surveillance of communicable diseases and related special health problems. a high-level meeting was held in brussels on 15 september to coordinate further steps in the eu's response to the ebola outbreak in west africa. in addition to the relevant commissioners and several ministers of health and development of the member states, the high-level coordinator of the un system for the ebola virus disease response, as well as representatives of the world health organisation and the ngo doctors without borders, attended the meeting. the meeting paved the way for greater coordination of the international effort needed to combat the epidemic. the european union's health ministers will discuss the issue at the informal ministerial meeting in milan on 22 and 23 september, with particular reference to the following actions: medium and long-term follow-up; information for travellers and citizens; medical evacuation; the need to share resources in complex emergencies; actions to improve the availability of ebola treatments and vaccines; the need for further support to affected countries, who and relevant non-governmental organisations, and the need for the eu to support the strengthening of global leadership and operational coordination of the who and un in the crisis response. president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i thought it important to speak about the commitment of the presidency and the council to coordinate the eu's efforts to help the affected countries and international organisations in the fight against this serious epidemic.
member of the commission. - mr president, we have heard a very comprehensive presentation from the council. i would like to contribute to the discussion by elaborating further on three points: first, the character of this epidemic; second, what we are doing at the commission to advance a coordinated response; and finally a few words about the approach we are taking to protect our own population, the citizens of europe. on the epidemic itself: it is unprecedented in two ways. firstly, this is a pandemic which is taking place in countries that had very weak health systems to begin with. in the past, if pandemics occurred they were mostly in middle-income or high-income countries where the health systems could be mobilised to respond. this is not the case now. secondly, at no time before has an ebola epidemic lasted so long, and it is not yet contained. so we are in a very unusual and very dramatic situation. as was mentioned, the un senior coordinator for the fight against ebola, dr david nabarro, who is extremely competent, told us that not only do we have 4 963 cases and 2 453 deaths today (that is actually as of yesterday) but that the most important and troubling fact is that figures for the number of cases are nearly doubling every three weeks. if we do not act decisively now, there are three major risks stemming from this. one is that in the three countries which are the most affected, guinea, liberia and sierra leone, the spread would be such that containing it would become extremely difficult. it is already difficult but it would be extremely difficult. secondly, we may not be able to protect other countries in the region from the spread of the epidemic. the worry then, of course, is that it may go further. and the third and most dangerous risk, i believe, is that the longer we fail to get on top of the epidemic the greater is the risk that the virus may mutate. what its impact would then be is hard to predict but it could be quite dramatic. we are not talking anymore just about a health emergency in the three countries; we are talking about an impact on their economies and their societies that is quite dramatic. growth rates have dropped significantly. we are worried about the political and security implications, and let us remember that these are countries that experienced civil wars in the 1990s and 2000s. they have just emerged from this, rebuilding their societies, and now they are being tremendously badly hit. we talk about fighting ebola on the front lines but this is not your usual humanitarian emergency where we can mobilise humanitarian staff, send them into the field and then they deal with the problem. this epidemic requires highly competent professionals in the health field who know how to deal with it. we are very constrained in terms of personnel, equipment and transport. going on to my second point: what are we in europe doing in terms of being on the front line in fighting ebola? of course we are mobilising money. i am proud to say that the commission, with eur 150 million, is leading in the financial response to this crisis. we have just received a figure from the united nations revised upwards: close to a billion dollars is now necessary, but we are putting our funding together and we will do more. on monday our member states had pledged up to eur 78 million. many of them, however, are working on raising their financial contributions so we can be more and more effective. much more important than money is mobilising assistance in kind and deploying teams. we have laboratories in the affected countries and, as we have heard, our member states are providing new hospitals and new treatment centres to provide beds. but let me tell you what the reaction of médecins sans frontières (msf) was to our numbers, which are in the high hundreds. they said high hundreds is good, but what we need is in the thousands if we want to stop the epidemic, because they are still sending people who are coming to treatment centres back to their communities, with all the risks that this creates. we are very focused on the critical issue of medical evacuation. for many health workers, one concern about going to the affected countries is ‘what would i do if i am impacted, would there be any help?’ we are working in europe to create a medical evacuation capacity so that that concern, and the health of medical workers, are addressed. last but not least, we understand how critical it is to invest in research, in vaccines and in treatment, and also to build a wall against any future ebola outbreaks. there was a discussion here in parliament on this topic with tonio borg in early september in the committee on the environment, public health and food safety. the third point is: what do we do about the safety of our own citizens? here we have received the message very loud and clear, and i want to split this into two points. one, we are saying let us stop the virus, isolate it and fight it back, but let us not isolate the countries. i want to pay tribute to brussels airlines and to air france, european companies that continue to fly back and forth to the region – absolutely essential. secondly, we have taken measures collectively to make sure that this is not going to bring the virus into europe. i can stand here in front of you and say we are doing this. a huge amount of work is going on at the moment to make sure that our laboratory system is ready to carry out testing in all member states and that those with fewer capabilities can count on the support of others; that we have suitable treatment facilities; that we coordinate our preventive measures; and also that we communicate with one voice so that we do not confuse people. i want to end by saying that i was very encouraged at the meeting on monday to see europe coming together as one. i heard a member state that would not normally say such a thing asking ‘please, coordinate usʼ. we want to act together and together we will act.

written. - in view of the situation of major structural changes in world trade flows that directly affect french automotive workers, i believe that eu financial assistance should be dynamic and made available as soon as possible to help workers to enter the labour market as soon as possible. the conditions of the egf regulation are met and i consider that france is entitled to a financial contribution under that regulation. to date, 21 applications for egf allocation related to the automotive sector have been received, 12 of which are based on the effects of globalisation on trade and 9 on the effects of the global financial and economic crisis. this package of services, adapted to the needs for which co-financing is sought, covers measures for redundant workers. i support the plan to provide interest-free loans to start-ups that could help participants to establish sustainable businesses. i would remind the importance of increasing the employment rate of all workers through tailored training programmes and the recognition of skills and competences acquired by the worker during his professional career. i welcome this decision as the harmonised package of tailor-made services has been designed in consultation with the national representatives of the intended beneficiaries and the social partners, and with the social policy of equality between women and men and the principle of non-discrimination.
written. - given that france has applied for financial assistance from the egf following the dismissal of 6 120 workers and that 2 357 persons are expected to be affected by measures relating to the operations of the manufacturing company peugeot automobiles, i consider it necessary to reduce the duration of the introduction period in order to allow the egf to act as quickly as possible. however, it is important to note that the egf was established to provide support for workers made redundant as a result of structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, and that it can only co-finance active labour market measures leading to long-term employment and should not replace activities for which undertakings are responsible under national law or collective agreements, nor restructuring measures. the plants concerned may undergo significant industrial conversion, which could encourage a stronger redistribution of labour if they exploit their potential for multimodal transport. in view of the above, i support the proposal and the egf should be mobilised in order to provide a financial contribution for the application submitted by france.
written. - i voted against the proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund, based on a request by spain for a financial contribution from the egf following 6 120 redundancies at peugeot citroën automobiles, with 2 357 workers expected to be covered by measures to be co-financed by the egf amounting to eur 12 704 605. in my view, such packages of measures are merely firefighting measures that offer no long-term solution to the redundancies on the one hand and to the poor economic situation in the crisis-hit sectors on the other. in particular, i believe that member states must provide their companies with a sound business framework that will enable them to compete in the global market, which presupposes the tax burden and the removal of bureaucratic barriers that hamper investment and business. in the case of france's request, i welcome the fact that the service includes measures for the granting of business start-up grants, but also a plan for the granting of interest-free loans for the establishment of companies. such measures should be the basis for any plan adopted after mass redundancies, rather than unpromising and precarious training measures. however, measures to encourage entrepreneurship must be one of the pillars of any economic recovery and employment policy, and not just one of the services offered to workers after their dismissal.

done at - on 6 march 2014, the council of the european union decided, on behalf of the european union and its member states, to conclude the additional protocol to the free trade agreement signed on 15 october 2009 between the member states, of the one part, and the republic of korea, of the other part. the european parliament has given its consent to the conclusion of this treaty. on 1 july 2013, the republic of croatia acceded to the union and became its 28th member. an additional protocol between the eu and the republic of korea to take account of the accession of croatia to the eu was signed and has been provisionally applied since 1 july 2013. i supported this rapporteur because the current council decision seeks to ensure, in accordance with the act of accession of croatia to the eu, that croatia as a member will continue to participate fully in the free trade between the eu and the republic of korea and, by signing the agreement, contribute to preserving the integrity of the union's internal market. the assent of the european parliament is a mandatory component in the completion of the ratification process of the additional protocol.
written. - i welcome the adaptation of the protocol to the eu-republic of korea free trade agreement to croatia's accession to the union. although korea is not one of the largest trade partners of the republic of croatia, trade between these two countries has significant potential for growth through investment in ports and infrastructure, export of croatian products and through an increase in the number of tourists, who visited croatia last year by as much as 58%. i would like to take this opportunity to recall that this agreement was adapted 15 months after croatia's accession and to point out that many other trade agreements concluded by the eu with third countries remained unadapted, including agreements with some of croatia's most important trading partners such as bih. by acceding to the european union, croatia has taken over the contractual and trade relations that the european union has with third countries and has automatically withdrawn from the existing trade agreements with third countries. however, third countries have not automatically adapted their agreements to croatia's accession to the eu, which has caused significant damage to the croatian economy. i hope that we will vote as soon as possible on the adaptation of the remaining trade agreements between the eu and third countries, so that croatian businesses can participate on an equal footing in the world market.

written. - as a croatian representative in the european parliament, i support the conclusion of an additional protocol to the existing free trade agreement. the conclusion of the protocol makes croatia a beneficiary of the bilateral trade agreement between south korea and the eu, the implementation of which should contribute to market development and economic growth in both countries. the agreement commits the eu member states and the republic of korea to eliminate 98,7% of customs duties on the value of trade for industrial and agricultural products over the next 5 years. croatia made a profit of around usd 8 million in 2012, mainly from exports of radiotelephony transmitters, turbocharged engines and starch production residues to korea, while in 2013 it made a profit of usd 12 million from exports of mainly the same products, which shows an increase in exports of 50%. on the other hand, korea is the main importer of passenger cars and motor vehicles and electrical appliances. i believe that this protocol opens up many opportunities for croatia, given the size of the market there. i welcome this decision, because the fta increases the turnover of the trade balances between the beneficiary countries and thus encourages the development of both economies. i would like to take this opportunity to call on those countries which have signed a free trade agreement with the eu and have not aligned it with croatia's accession to the eu to do so.

written. twenty-five years have passed since a historic event that marked a turning point, a new beginning and a european future for many member states. human courage has succeeded in overcoming the concrete blocks and has set in motion processes of which many citizens, not just german citizens, can be proud. unfortunately, today we are witnessing some new "walls" that are not exclusively concrete, but at least equally effective in keeping many people away from their basic rights. the berlin wall serves as a symbol of the breaking down of barriers among people who have come together to realize their rights, but it should also be a reminder and an inspiration to all who are able to decide that fundamental human rights are no longer threatened by any physical, economic or security divides. twenty-five years after the berlin wall fell and the promise of freedom for millions of people, we cannot allow some new "walls" to keep millions more trapped in poverty and hopelessness.
the fall of the berlin wall on 9 november 1989 ended the bloc division in europe and made possible the reunification of germany. the democratic transition has begun in central and eastern europe, and the lives of today's generation have been radically changed. there is a wide range of political and sociological interpretations of the causes, consequences and significance of the fall of the wall and the collapse of communism. the most important aspect is that the process has been launched towards the realization of the freedom and democracy that the peoples of central and eastern europe dreamed of, who were, by historical circumstances, part of the former communist bloc. the way is also open for the enlargement of the european union. croatia also became part of the continental political project in 2013. membership of the european family was achieved after demanding reforms, but above all thanks to the sacrifices of croatian defenders in the patriotic war. these days also marks the 23rd anniversary of the fall of vukovar - the city symbol of croatian freedom. in view of the fact that 2014 also marks the 100th anniversary of the outbreak of the first world war and the 75th anniversary of the outbreak of the second world war, which brought the greatest tragedies to mankind, it is of the utmost importance to put an end to the hybrid aggression against ukraine that undermines the fundamental values of the global order and international law. the creation of new frozen conflicts could lead to divisions that return europe to the time before 1989.
written. the fall of the berlin wall 25 years ago was a moment of optimism for me as a young man and for my entire generation. new opportunities such as public speaking and freedom of movement and expression have been extremely stimulating across europe. the fall of the berlin wall has led to the construction and restoration of democracies in eastern and south-eastern europe, which has opened up a vast space for the development of civil society, the economy and citizenship. although yugoslavia was not behind the iron curtain, the cold war was its reality. as a buffer zone between east and west, it felt locally the omnipresent global threats. is there still anyone in europe today who thinks about building nuclear shelters? for us, it was just a regular thing. then and now, in the region and in the world, there are forces constantly present who want to build walls. it's not just physical walls, but also various energy, cultural and financial walls of blackmail. sometimes it seems easier to build walls than to build social inclusion. the european union has great potential and power to prevent conflicts in its neighbourhood and to connect states and societies at all levels. the memory of this momentous event of the fall of the berlin wall should be an example and an inspiration to all generations that freedom is the right of every individual not only in our community but also in the whole world.
written. the fall of the berlin wall, the most powerful symbol of the collapse of the eastern bloc, radically changed the world, but also the world public's view of communism and the communist system and created the conditions for democratization and the removal of the iron curtains from the north to the south of europe. coming from croatia, which was under communism for 45 years, i sympathize with and understand the plight of people who lived under that totalitarian system throughout central and eastern europe. the following years saw the collapse of the soviet union and the sfr yugoslavia, and numerous nations gained independence, while the revolutions of 1989 marked a change in the balance of power as well as the beginning of a post-communist era and democracy. in most of the new states, the governments are engaged in establishing a stable market economy, and croatia is at the same time facing war and aggression, while numerous fallen defenders have embedded their lives in the foundations of modern croatia. it is a pity that today there are politicians who look back with nostalgia on that authoritarian system. in the light of the european parliament's resolutions on the need for international condemnation of the crimes of totalitarian communist regimes, i call on the commission to persevere in condemning those who still today glorify and highlight the symbols of totalitarian systems, including communism, taking into account the evil and injustice that system has brought to citizens throughout europe and beyond.
mr president, while welcoming the commissioners, i would like to mention in the discussion of the northern ireland peace process two other important agreements that have ended conflicts in two other european countries. the dayton and erdut agreements marked the end of the war in bosnia and herzegovina and my homeland croatia. summing up their similarities and differences, i would say that both agreements brought peace, but the erdut agreement ensured the full integration of the speech area, the constitutional and legal order of the country, while dayton unfortunately did not allow the construction of a unified and functional state. by the erdut agreement between croatia and serbia, the croatian territory of the danube was peacefully integrated with the mediation of the international community. it was a sort of introduction to croatia's european future. its success, apart from peaceful reintegration, is represented by the fact that over two-thirds of the serbian population remained to live in the mentioned area. that is why i want the spirit of the erdut agreement, as well as the good friday agreement, these examples of win-win concepts in areas affected by long-standing conflicts to be reflected in further agreements between, for example, belgrade and pristina or why not moscow and kiev.

member of the commission. - mr president, i am very pleased and honoured to be here as commissioner for regional policy and i thank the committee on regional development for this important question, which allows me to explain where we stand with our cohesion policy programming and the measures that we need to take in order to guarantee smooth and fast completion of the process. let us start with good news. as you know, all partnership agreements and 39 cohesion policy programmes have been adopted to date, including 24 investment for growth and jobs programmes where regio is in the lead, 14 where employment is in the lead, and one european territorial cooperation programme. the first rural development and maritime and fisheries programmes will be adopted by the end of this year and the rest will follow in 2015. as you said, the 2014-2020 legislative package for cohesion policy was adopted very late, in december 2013, six months later than the corresponding package in 2006 for the period 2007-2013, so this late adoption of the multiannual framework and regulation left no time for preparation of the programming period starting on 1 january 2014. expenditure is eligible as from 1 january 2014, which means that member states do not need to wait for the programmes to be adopted. they can start implementation of activities in sectors that are not subject to debate with the commission. in fact, in many regions, calls for proposals and project selection processes have already started, and some of the operations to be supported are already ongoing. of course, procedures and projects that started before adoption of the programmes will need to be confirmed and validated by the monitoring committees, once established, and will need to comply with the regulation. you ask about the main difficulties encountered when discussing operational programmes with member states; and, of course, circumstances and issues are different from one member state to another, so i do not think it would be appropriate in such a limited time to give details. but to summarise, i can say that the debates were mainly on a handful of recurrent issues: the insufficient logic of the intervention foreseen, and therefore the need to strengthen the link between needs and challenges, identified inter alia in the country-specific recommendations, and between results to be achieved corresponding to indicators and actions to be supported; the lack of concentration of investment priorities, the fulfilment of ex ante conditionalities, and finally, of course, the importance of having robust strategies in place to enhance administrative capacity. moving to the question of the programmes that still need to be adopted, we consider that more than half of all cohesion policy programmes will have been adopted either by the end of the year or under the carryover procedure by march at the latest. in order to preserve the 2014 commitments for the remaining programmes, and those that will not be ready for adoption by the end of this year, the commission intends to present a revision of the mff by early february 2015. we hope that we can count on the european parliament and the council to help us secure early adoption of this mff revision and the related amending budget before 4 may 2015. the internal commission procedures have also been streamlined in order to allow them to carry over as many programmes as possible. however, the commission will not compromise quality over speed. the programmes which set the framework for investment for the next seven years must build on solid strategies so that european taxpayer can be assured of getting the most effective use of their contributions. finally, i would like to assure you that the backlog of 2013 unpaid claims for cohesion policy – and i know mr van nistelrooij will ask me about that – will not affect the start of the new period, as the newly adopted programmes have immediately received pre-financing. i had an intense discussion with the commissioner for the budget and with other colleagues in order to find a solution for these unpaid claims. however, approval of the third amending budget for 2014 and the budget for 2015 by the budgetary authority as foreseen by the commission remains essential in order to reduce the amount of unpaid claims for the 2007-2013 period for this and next year. thank you very much once again and i am looking forward to hearing from you.

mr president, i share the concern about the increase in unemployment and poverty in the european union and the growing disparities between member states. achieving the employment and poverty reduction targets must indeed be our priority. but i don't think we're going to get there by increasing the regulatory burden, which to the extent it does is stifling small and medium-sized enterprises, which are the engines of economic growth and whose stability and good business are the main drivers of employment. a good number of colleagues are advocating for more welfare payments to fight poverty, while rejecting fiscal consolidation. the croatian example shows that without fiscal consolidation and tax relief for companies, any effect is absent, as the closure of private companies leads to a budget deficit that would only be deepened by unrealistically high social contributions. it's not the way to equality or prosperity, but debt slavery.

member of the commission. - madam president, commissioner vella regrets that he is not able to be in strasbourg today. he is in brussels at the fisheries council, but he has asked me to present the views of the commission on this file to you. i would like, first of all, to thank ms ayuso and ms herranz garcía for their excellent and efficient work on this particular file. when presenting these political guidelines to parliament in july, president juncker made clear that one of the aims of the new commission is to reinforce the eu as a strong global actor. the eu accession to the cites convention is to be seen in this context. the cites convention aims to make international trade in wildlife species sustainable. it is a very operational and efficient instrument that regulates millions of cross-border movements of animals, plants and commodities derived from them, such as timber, leather goods, medicines, cosmetics and food products. in total, we are talking about 35 000 species that are covered by cites. this wide scope, combined with the legally binding nature of its decisions and its robust compliance mechanism, makes the cites convention a critical tool to address the overexploitation of natural resources, which is one of the biggest threats to biodiversity today. the cites convention stands at the crossroads of environment, trade and development. these are all areas in which the eu is a leading actor on the international scene. these are also areas in which the eu has strong legislation and policies. the eu’s accession to the convention will reflect its leading role, and it will increase the eu’s visibility and accountability. the situation will be similar to the other organisations such as the wto, the fao or the convention on biological diversity, of which the eu has been a full member for many years. in operational terms, the way we prepare for cites meetings will not change much after the eu accession, as there is a well-established practice to agree on common eu positions before each meeting. however, the eu will gain visibility at the cites meetings, as eu positions will be expressed by the eu on matters of eu competence. the eu will also be able to participate fully in the various bodies set up under the convention and contribute to its annual budget. this accession comes at a particularly important time. cites has recently engaged much more in regulating international trade in marine and timber species. these are very valuable commodities traded in large amounts. the eu has pushed for these, and our accession to cites will allow us to increase our investment further to ensure that the international timber and fish trades are legal and sustainable. cites is also at the forefront of the fight against wildlife trafficking, a problem which i know is important to this parliament. the current dramatic surge in wildlife trafficking calls for a strong response from the international community. at its last meeting in july, the cites standing committee adopted very concrete measures targeting the countries most involved in wildlife trafficking, particularly in ivory, rhino horns and rosewood. these measures need to be implemented within strict deadlines, and failure to do so could result in the adoption of trade sanctions. increasingly, cites is also engaging in close cooperation with international organisations like the un office on drugs and crime, and interpol, which also specialise in combating organised crime. the eu must play its role in these global efforts, and the accession to cites is a very concrete step towards facilitating this. to conclude, i would stress that the eu’s accession to cites will reinforce both the eu as a global player and cites as an essential multilateral instrument for sustainable development. the commission is aware of the interest of parliament in these matters, and we count on your support in finally making it possible for the eu to become a full party to cites.

president of the council. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union is the world's largest donor of humanitarian aid, and bilateral assistance from the member states is a considerable part of that effort. the european union member states alone have provided almost one and a half billion euros in humanitarian assistance since the beginning of the syrian crisis in 2011. this is in addition to the €666 million in humanitarian aid from the eu budget provided by the commission. as honourable members are well aware, the council has just approved, with parliament, the 2014 amending budget, making an additional eur 214 million available to the commission's humanitarian aid budget for this year. a large part of this amount is used for the european union's response to the syrian crisis. this is a clear demonstration of our commitment to providing humanitarian aid to those in need, particularly those affected by the syrian crisis. yesterday the council adopted conclusions on the situation in syria and we expressed our grave concern at the dramatic funding shortfall in response to the un appeals for 2014, which has led to the temporary suspension of assistance to syrian refugees by the world food programme and we called on the international community to step up funding in view of the winter and in response to the upcoming appeals for 2015. but we have not only asked others, the member states have been among the main donors who have responded immediately to the urgent appeal of the world food programme for funding for syria. for example, the netherlands, germany, ireland and belgium have collectively contributed more than $14 million. together with the commission's contribution from the eu budget, this brings the eu's collective response to this emergency appeal to more than eur 20 million. we are pleased that this has now helped to fill the gap experienced by the world food programme and that food assistance for 1.7 million syrian refugees can resume as planned. it remains tragic that in a crisis of the scale of the syrian crisis there can barely be enough funds to meet all the needs of the internally displaced. many of those who had to flee syria often did so with nothing but the clothes they were wearing. but we can certainly make sure that we do not add to their suffering. the council and the member states cannot accept reductions in food aid for those who have lost everything. we have coordinated very closely within the council, between the member states and also with the commission, the response to this unprecedented crisis. we make sure there is no overlap in our collective response as we try to fill, as best we can, the gaps in global funding. in this context, i would also like to point out that the member states of the european union are one of the main donors to the world food programme. even before the recent emergency appeal, eu member states had paid more than €150 million to the world food programme in 2014 for its action in the context of the syrian crisis alone. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we consider the world food programme to be one of our main executive partners in the provision of humanitarian assistance by the european union. both as the european union and as member states, we have a long tradition of cooperation on a bilateral basis. we will therefore ensure, together with the world food programme, that appropriate measures are taken in terms of both financing and planning. we must ensure that deficiencies such as we have seen do not happen again. we owe it to all the people we try to help, first and foremost to the innocent victims of the terrible war in syria.
member of the commission.– mr president, i am grateful for the opportunity to address this important issue today. there is no question but that the syrian crisis is unprecedented. both in terms of its humanitarian consequences and for its financial implications. an immediate reaction by international donors is a precondition for avoiding a further deterioration in the situation. a comprehensive response to the crisis cannot be built on our normal budgets. we must work together to make a strong eu response possible. we have a collective responsibility to find the means to achieve this goal. the wfpʼs decision to cut back food assistance is a reminder of the overwhelming impact of the biggest humanitarian tragedy of our times. i want to underline that the eu as a whole is responding to the syrian crisis needs. we are responding to the call by the wfp which has resumed its aid scheme to syrian refugees. i want to express my sincere appreciation for the broad support of this parliament in this crisis. the european union has led the international response to the syrian crisis. we have provided more than eur 3.1 billion. of this, eur 681 million has come from the commission’s humanitarian budget, with eur 120 million provided for wfpʼs operations in syria and neighbouring countries. the wfp is our second largest humanitarian partner after the unhcr. we are 2014 is up to eur 18 million, on top of the eur 61 million allocated in december 2013. we will continue our efforts to mobilise additional resources. it is no accident that a few days ago both the wfp and valerie amos from ocha, who is very well known, expressed their appreciation to the eu for our generous humanitarian support. it is true that the wfp has by far the biggest needs in this crisis, estimated to reach usd 1.8 billion this year. this amount goes beyond the usd 1.6 billion needs of the unhcr. the fact that approximately only 60% of these needs are matched with funding is a major problem. unfortunately the wfp is only one of the many partners in desperate need of funding. for this reason we have repeatedly warned the donor community that the gap between needs and funding is unfortunately not sustainable. syria is the biggest crisis we face today but it is not the only crisis. think of iraq, the central african republic, south sudan, etc. all of these crises have stretched humanitarian budgets beyond their limits. certainly money will never be enough; therefore we need more cost-effective and more targeted operations from humanitarian partners. this also applies to the wfp. this year we will finish with eur 165 million in humanitarian assistance for the syrian crisis. this is already less than half of the exceptional eur 350 million we managed to mobilise in 2012. next year our commissionʼs initial humanitarian funding will be down to 100 million. there will be additional money forthcoming soon. i will use all the leverage i have to achieve that. but my efforts alone, unfortunately, are not enough. we need strong collective action for next year. we expect needs of usd 7.2 billion for the syrian crisis alone. this is a substantial increase compared to the record figure of usd 6 billion for this year. the syrian crisis will remain a top priority in the years to come. the whole region is feeling its impact. we have to find ways to increase funding and make it sustainable, otherwise it will be a short fix. we must adopt a long-term approach. we must continue honouring our pledges. it is not only our moral duty, it is also a question of life or death for millions of syrian refugees. as you know, a few days ago i came back from a joint mission with vice-president federica mogherini and commissioner johannes hahn to turkey. there we also visited refugee camps along the syrian border. the situation on the ground is overwhelming. cuts in food assistance will be felt there first. it is our collective responsibility to stop this from happening. we must work together to avoid this situation. at the end of the day, however, what is needed for the syrian crisis is a political solution. un special envoy de mistura has our full support in this regard. it is a support reflected yesterday in the foreign affairs council conclusions.

written. due to the exceptionally high level of additional resources to be paid by certain member states as a result of the alignment of own resources contributions based on gni during 2014, the commission submitted to the council a proposal for a council regulation amending the regulation on the system of the european communities' own resources. i welcome the commission's proposal as it gives member states the flexibility needed to pay the amount resulting from the reconciliation of national contributions (own resources) on the basis of value added tax and gross national income, if the total amount is extremely high. i would also point out the importance of communication and of taking account of the views of the european court of auditors. it is also important that eurostat adheres to the recommendation of the court of auditors as regards its verification methodology in order to fully respect the principle of equal treatment of member states in practice. therefore, i support the report.
written. i support the proposal to amend regulation (ec, euratom) no 1150/2000 because the provision of large sums of money can certainly represent (and does represent) fiscal and other pressures for economically weaker member states. if this proposal leads to real aid rather than just prescribed aid, it will be a great relief to some member states in the current economic crisis. we can and must use every means at our disposal to alleviate the situation, but equally, those means must not be used when they are not necessary. efficiency and solidarity are the fundamental principles of the european union.
written. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund to provide an amount of eur 50 million in the 2015 budget to allow for a faster and more efficient response to major natural disasters during the following year. the fund was established to deal with major natural disasters as efficiently as possible and to provide financial assistance to affected countries and regions, i.e. eu member states and acceding countries, as quickly and effectively as possible. i think it is extremely important that member states and acceding countries receive financial assistance at the time of a disaster faster than is possible under the normal procedure. such support by the eu carries a clear political message of solidarity while providing assistance to those in need.
in the last three years, natural disasters around the world have claimed more than 40,000 lives and caused economic losses worth some $350 billion. in 2012, the largest economic losses, totaling $18 billion, were caused by floods that affected germany, the czech republic, and neighboring countries. this year, the storm and its aftermath, andreas, hit germany and france in july, causing an estimated $3.8 billion in economic damage. the biggest natural disaster of the year, cyclone donat, hit croatia, italy, bosnia and herzegovina and serbia in the spring, causing catastrophic consequences. the consequences in croatia were unimaginable, with over 15,000 people evacuated and total damage estimated at over 220 million euros. these are just some of the natural disasters that have struck europe and left behind damages that have not been repaired to this day. i therefore support this proposal to mobilise eur 50 million from the european union solidarity fund. this money is needed to repair damaged areas and prevent further damage. the consequences of increasingly frequent natural disasters are enormous, not only in terms of loss of life but also in terms of loss of homes, jobs, industries, and economies that once thrived in the area.
written. i support the decision to mobilise up to eur 50 million from the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2013 for the payment of advances and other appropriations. since its creation in 2002, the fund has disbursed more than eur 3.5 billion to help with the recovery of 56 disasters, clearly demonstrating the fund's legitimacy and its importance to the european union. although the very existence of the fund is a sign of the european union's unity and solidarity, i believe that the disbursement of funds should be more effective in order to recover as quickly as possible from the consequences of natural disasters. the increasingly large and costly impact of climate change is making it clear that the solidarity fund will become an increasingly important eu financial instrument. the european union must change its approach to climate change as soon as possible. as a community, we must direct our public policies towards preventing climate change. our collective resources in this approach can have a much greater impact while focusing only on repairing the damage is unsustainable in the long run.
the european union solidarity fund has a protection and recovery role in places affected by various disasters. the amount of eur 50 000 000 is secured for this fund and should be included in the 2015 payment budget on the basis of the principle of solidarity in order to address the greatest needs. i support the mobilisation of the solidarity fund because it provides solutions to natural disasters that are beyond the control and predictability of humans, and which leave behind them a loss of life and material consequences. the purpose of this tool is to show solidarity with the people of the region affected by the disaster. it allows for a faster and more efficient recovery of the affected areas and i therefore support the report.
written. solidarity is one of the fundamental principles of the european union. it is in these times of severe natural disasters that we have the opportunity to apply this principle in practice. this is one of the reasons why i supported this initiative, as it provides assistance through the solidarity fund to member states which, in addition to suffering the severe consequences of natural disasters, are in a poor economic situation. the commission shall be assisted by the european parliament and the council. natural disasters have become more frequent in recent years and, in addition to mobilising the solidarity fund, i call on all member states to make use of the eu funds available to them to prevent natural disasters as much as possible.

written. i voted out of the resolution on the draft commission regulation supplementing the regulation as regards the classification of serious infringements of union rules and amending annex iii to directive 2006/22/ec, as the commission proposal is not sufficiently clear or sufficiently detailed. roads are the lifeblood of the european economy and road transport is the lifeline of the european economy. we are witnessing a number of problems of unfair competition and so-called 'social dumping' in the trucking industry. there are many examples of great differences in regulations between member states and as i support the idea of standardising regulations, because standardising those regulations relies on the free movement of people and goods, i did not support the proposal for a regulation. by taking the no position, i wanted to make clear my support for all those who are calling for the european commission to come out with far clearer rules to increase road safety.
written. i support the motion for a resolution rejecting the proposal for a commission regulation on the classification of serious infringements of union rules. the 2009 regulation defines four criteria that road freight transport service providers must fulfil in order to be authorised to provide those services. the 'good repute' criterion was established with the aim of ensuring the ethical behaviour of entrepreneurs. in order to ensure consistent application of the rules in all member states, it is necessary that the list defining the categories of infringement is complete and clear. i do not think that is the case with the proposal which has been sent to us from the commission. at this stage, the practical implementation of the regulation is very uneven within the european union because the definition of infringements is left to the national authorities responsible for this area. this amendment to the regulation does not, unfortunately, ensure the necessary harmonisation of implementation. since the proposed list is limited to those actions which result in death or serious injury, i consider that the list is incomplete. given that the regulation provides that data on serious infringements of the rules will be available for electronic exchange between member states by 1 january 2016 at the latest and that the lack of harmonised rules for the practical application of the rules already creates obstacles for businesses, i consider it necessary to speed up the drafting of the full text and its implementation.

written. i voted out of the resolution on the draft commission directive laying down the method of calculation and the reporting requirements under directive 98/70/ec on the quality of petrol and diesel fuels on the grounds that it calls for the withdrawal of the draft council directive which certainly does not achieve the highest necessary environmental protection standards but also aligns the need to reduce co2 emissions with the current needs of the fuel production and distribution sector. the directive also takes into account the non-conformity of the manufacturers' technology and takes into account the practical implementation of future measures through the differentiation of fuel types. this will allow the implementation of the 6% co2 reduction target to start in the short term. the adoption of the resolution would prolong the procedure without precise deadlines and would in the short term cause greater damage to the environment. in voting, i took into account the needs of the croatian economy and the previous positions of the croatian government as well as the need of the estonian oil industry to be brought into problems that would have political implications in addition to economic ones.
written. the methods set out in this report do not provide a clear and precise formula for calculating greenhouse gas emissions into the environment. the reason is that the documents submitted do not allow a precise assessment of the origin, the volume, the type and the life cycle of the greenhouse gases. i call on the commission to adopt implementing measures relating to the greenhouse gas monitoring and reduction mechanism. the commission is currently examining the methodology for calculating greenhouse gas emissions from fuels and other non-biological energy sources. in this context, i consider that the annual reports of suppliers should be harmonised before being submitted to the member states and then the member states should do the same in the commission's reporting process, all for the purpose of high-quality and simple monitoring and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions in the union. for all the above reasons, i have not endorsed this report.
written. while the proposal for this directive aims in principle to reduce greenhouse gas intensity, imposes a decarbonisation obligation, requires suppliers to calculate life cycle greenhouse gas emissions for biofuels, requires the use of the same average default values for all fossil raw materials, i consider that the methodology does not take into account all the necessary parameters that would guarantee further emission reductions or environmental integrity, and i support the re-drafting of the council directive. i agree to the submission of the request for disaggregated average greenhouse gas intensity values and for reporting by raw material type for petrol and diesel fuels and for suppliers to be allowed to report on actual values. for the reasons stated above, i did not support this proposal.
written. i abstained from voting on the resolution on the commission delegated regulation adopting a discard plan for the baltic sea because i am fundamentally opposed to the fishing of small fish. although the alde group was for, i decided to be related because it expressed my view that small-scale fishing, especially in the high seas, is a serious problem. i was basically advocating for a ban on fishing for cod in the baltic sea up to a size of 38 cm. today, cod can be caught as early as when the fish reaches a length of 35 cm. a difference of just 3 centimeters significantly affects the overall size of the cod. i have also expressed my views on the protection of the sea and the fish stocks. in many conversations with mr walter dodich, i have come to the conclusion that premature fishing significantly reduces the fish stock and causes irreversible damage in the long term.
written. one of the main objectives of the new common fisheries policy (cfp) is to phase out discarding in all eu fisheries by introducing a landing obligation. the intention is to make better use of available resources and to respond to public expectations to put an end to the practice of discarding surplus fish back into the sea. the high levels of discarded catches have been identified as an important reason for the lack of environmental sustainability of the common fisheries policy and i have therefore supported this report.
written. the challenge of sustainable fishing is to bring factors under control that can be controlled during fishing to ensure that there are enough individuals in the sea to naturally replenish the population. factors that cannot be influenced are population biomass increase and natural mortality, and these depend on environmental conditions and biological characteristics of the species (rejuvenation and growth). the commission has also concluded that the fishing opportunities available to the union are limited to the areas referred to in article 4 of regulation (eu) no 1380/2013. since cod, herring and papalina have strong biological interactions, they are extremely important components of the baltic ecosystem. the ecological conditions in the baltic can have a strong impact on the productivity of baltic fish stocks, in particular cod and parrotfish, and the council decision on tacs therefore seeks to reduce quotas (7% for the western part of the baltic and 22% for the eastern part) with a view to conserving those species. this was regulated on 1 january 2014 by the regulation of the european parliament and of the council of 11 december 2013 on the common fisheries policy. in this respect, i support the commission's proposal to adopt a discard plan for the baltic sea. i believe that the sustainable exploitation of marine biological resources would be more effectively achieved through a multiannual approach to fisheries management and that it should be based on transparent and objective criteria, including those of an environmental, social and economic nature.
written. i did not support the regulation which objects to the plan adopted by the commission for discarding catches in the baltic sea because that plan could potentially endanger the reproductive capacity of that species, a worrying fact to which parliament has reacted. the council has decided to reduce the quota to protect the species, as there are fewer cod in the sea at the moment. the mere fact that the minimum cod reference size has also been reduced from 38 cm to 35 cm is sufficient to reconsider the commission's plan and therefore the current regulation needs to be amended in order to achieve a more efficient and realistic plan and to minimise the damage and the protection of the species.

written. i voted in favour of the resolution on the renewal of the eu internal security strategy to take effect for the next four years, as the current internal security strategy (iss) needs to be thoroughly evaluated and updated. the new strategy will cover existing security threats, but also all new ones that have not existed until now, but have become present at international level and, due to their complexity, require better cooperation between member states to deal with them adequately. these include, for example, internet safety for children and adults, data protection and privacy, human trafficking, the fight against organised crime, corruption, terrorism, money laundering, various crimes and more. i believe that the future updated internal security strategy will better encourage operational cooperation between member states and a european law enforcement culture.
