mr president, i regard the joint resolution of the european parliament on the recognition in principle of palestinian statehood as the beginning or continuation of a historically important process, not as its arrest or relativization. the resolution represents a welcome compromise between the main political groups that share the same goal but differ in the process of achieving it. it finally opens the way for a more engaged european diplomacy in a part of the world that has been particularly devastated this year by old conflicts and new brutality. i see the future of an independent palestine not as a new factor in the emergence of a long-term conflict, but as a new possibility for a more effective search for a more lasting peaceful solution. i would quote an israeli politician who recently said that israel should not exhaust itself waiting for the ideal partner on the palestinian side to make a lasting peace agreement. on the other hand, our resolution raises the expectation that the palestinian representatives will use the european parliament's confidence responsibly and contribute to the realisation of the concept of two states that renounce violence and terrorism and cooperate in peace.
mr. president, i voted in favor of this resolution because it reflects my position, as well as the position of european citizens on the establishment of two states to be achieved through peace negotiations. in particular, statehood requires legal and orderly functioning that excludes support for organisations that can be called terrorist or that are guided by the principles of any form of fundamentalism, including religious fundamentalism. hamas' behaviour, its resistance to finding non-violent solutions and its support for attacks on israeli territory and its use of its own people as human shields are the biggest obstacles to the continuation of peace talks. the cessation of armed attacks by the palestinian authority and the resumption of peace negotiations are therefore a precondition for the recognition of a palestinian state. the parties shall also allow humanitarian organisations to deliver humanitarian aid to the palestinian population without hindrance in accordance with the geneva convention. i take this opportunity to call once again on the opposing sides to continue peace negotiations and to find solutions that will secure and enable israel and palestinian statehood and solutions that will ensure lasting peace in that area.
written. i supported the resolution on the recognition of palestinian statehood because i believe that the middle east peace process has been blocked for a long time and there is no sign that the situation will change soon. the introduction of new elements, such as the international recognition of a palestinian state, can provide the necessary impetus for finding a just solution and achieving lasting peace in the middle east.
written. i voted in favour of the resolution on the recognition of palestinian statehood because it is a very balanced resolution and offers the possibility of creating an area of peace in a region that has been troubled for decades in the middle east. the existence of sovereign states of israel and palestine based on mutual recognition and good interstate relations is the foundation for peace in the middle east. it was important to me that in recent months many prominent supporters of this resolution in israel have come forward and that there has been a debate within the alde group and in the european parliament. i was also motivated by the desire to make the european union more present in this long-standing conflict in political and security terms. i consider that to be in the direct interest of the european union.
the israeli-palestinian conflict is the central conflict in the middle east. considering the conflict began in 1948 and the fact that it has never ended, it is considered one of the most severe conflicts of our time. the political perspective and processes in the palestinian and israeli territories are lacking and the resumption of peace negotiations is a priority. i support the resolution because it calls for peace and the resumption of peace negotiations which should also result in the recognition of a palestinian state within the 1967 borders (the so-called green line) with its capital in jerusalem as the joint capital of the two states. we are aware that the creation of such a state is the key to a lasting, just and sustainable peace and to resolving the conflict that has generated instability in that part of the world for decades. however, this does not mean that the state should be recognized without any obligations by the palestinians and their self-government. the state is not only a right, but also a great obligation and responsibility. we need to be sure that the palestinians will lead their state in the desired direction and maintain peace and that the palestinians and the israelis will sit down at the table, recognize each other and agree on all the fundamental issues of the conflict.
written. the worrying situation in the middle east continues to be the subject of our discussions, with the increase in tension and violence in the region and the increase in the number of terrorist attacks. i congratulate all the negotiators who constructively articulated the compromise text of the joint resolution of the political groups on which the ep voted today, which i co-signed. the key is a principled political message that meets israel's security and palestine's aspirations for its statehood. in line with the views of the european people's party, i am in favour of the concept of two states based on the 1967 borders with jerusalem as their capital, living side by side in peace and security. the european parliament has also called for the eu to take action to ensure that the palestinian people are not left behind. the only way to achieve this idea is to have an agreement between the parties to the conflict, first of all israel and palestine, who must decide to coexist and to have a long-term agreement. the resolution's key message is that hamas should follow fatah's position (i.e. the 1993 plo commitment) on recognizing the state of israel. the eu's main objective must be to find a solution to the conflict that contributes to the security of israel and ensures an independent, democratic and viable palestine and contributes to peace in the middle east region.
